lesson_title: The Lunar Disc: Features, Rotation and Libration
claim: Soviet Luna 3 photographed the far side of the Moon in 1959
notes: Luna 3 transmitted the first photographs of the lunar far side on 7 October 1959. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Earth-Moon-Sun: Scale, Eclipses and Tides
claim: The Sun's tidal influence on Earth is roughly 46% as strong as the Moon's
notes: Standard textbook value. The Sun's tidal force is approximately 46% of the Moon's despite far greater mass because tidal force scales as M/d^3 and the Sun is ~390 times further away.

lesson_title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
claim: Eratosthenes (~240 BCE) measured Earth's circumference as 40,000 km using a 7.2° shadow angle between Syene and Alexandria (~800 km apart)
notes: Method and result are accurate. Modern Earth circumference ~40,075 km. The 7.2° angle and 800 km separation are standard values used in all accounts of this measurement.

lesson_title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
claim: Aristarchus (c. 310–230 BCE) proposed a heliocentric model 'nearly 1,800 years before Copernicus'
notes: Aristarchus active ~270 BCE, Copernicus published 1543 CE — gap is ~1,813 years. 'Nearly 1,800 years' is accurate.

lesson_title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
claim: Axial precession period is approximately 26,000 years
notes: IAU value: ~25,772 years. Stated as '~26,000 years' which is standard rounding for educational contexts.

lesson_title: Ancient Astronomy: Eratosthenes, Aristarchus and Precession
claim: Vega will be the pole star in about 12,000 years
notes: Vega (α Lyrae) will be close to the north celestial pole in approximately 13,000 years (year ~14,000 CE). '~12,000 years' is slightly short but within acceptable rounding for a GCSE course.

lesson_title: Time: Sidereal vs Solar Days and the Equation of Time
claim: Sidereal day is approximately 23 hours 56 minutes
notes: Precise value: 23 h 56 m 4.091 s. The stated value is correct to the nearest minute.

lesson_title: Phases, Seasons and Time Zones
claim: Sidereal month ≈ 27.3 days; synodic month ≈ 29.5 days
notes: Precise values: sidereal 27.321 days, synodic 29.530 days. Both stated values are correct to the given precision.

lesson_title: Phases, Seasons and Time Zones
claim: John Harrison's H4 chronometer (completed 1759) solved the longitude problem
notes: H4 was completed 1759 and demonstrated its accuracy in 1761–1762 sea trials. Statement is accurate.

lesson_title: Observing the Sun and Planets in Motion
claim: Mercury's maximum elongation from the Sun is 28°; Venus can reach 47°
notes: Mercury's maximum elongation varies ~18°–28° (orbital eccentricity). 28° is the correct maximum. Venus maximum elongation varies ~45°–47°. Both values are correct.

lesson_title: Observing the Sun and Planets in Motion
claim: Venus transits: last pair was 2004 and 2012; next is 2117
notes: Venus transits occurred 8 June 2004 and 5–6 June 2012. Next transit: 10–11 December 2117. All dates confirmed.

lesson_title: Observing the Sun and Planets in Motion
claim: Perseids meteor shower peaks around 11–13 August
notes: Peak typically 11–13 August annually. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Early Models of the Solar System
claim: Ptolemy c. 100–170 CE compiled the Almagest using epicycles and deferents
notes: Dates and description are accurate. The Almagest (Μαθηματικὴ Σύνταξις) is correctly attributed.

lesson_title: Early Models of the Solar System
claim: Stellar parallax was not detected until 1838
notes: Friedrich Bessel measured the parallax of 61 Cygni in 1838. First confirmed stellar parallax measurement.

lesson_title: Planetary Motion and Gravity
claim: Copernicus (1473–1543) published De revolutionibus in 1543
notes: Published the year of his death, 1543. Correct.

lesson_title: Planetary Motion and Gravity
claim: Tycho Brahe (1546–1601) observed from 'the island of Hven in Denmark'
notes: Hven (now Ven, Sweden) was then under Danish crown. Brahe built Uraniborg and Stjerneborg there from 1576. Calling it 'in Denmark' reflects its historical political status.

lesson_title: Planetary Motion and Gravity
claim: Kepler published his laws in 1609 and 1619
notes: First and Second Laws: Astronomia Nova (1609). Third Law: Harmonices Mundi (1619). Correct.

lesson_title: Planetary Motion and Gravity
claim: Newton (1643–1727) published Principia Mathematica in 1687
notes: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica published 5 July 1687. Newton's dates (New Style): 4 Jan 1643 – 31 Mar 1727. All correct.

lesson_title: Planetary Motion and Gravity
claim: Kepler's Third Law worked example: Mars T = 1.881 years gives r = 1.52 AU
notes: Mars orbital period 686.97 days = 1.8808 years. Semi-major axis 1.524 AU. Calculation r^3 = T^2 = 1.881^2 = 3.538, r = ∛3.538 ≈ 1.52 AU. Correct.

lesson_title: Exploring the Moon: Origin, Far Side and Apollo
claim: Apollo 11 landed at the Sea of Tranquility on 20 July 1969
notes: Eagle landed at 20:17 UTC on 20 July 1969. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Exploring the Moon: Origin, Far Side and Apollo
claim: The Apollo programme returned 382 kg of lunar samples; six successful landings (Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17)
notes: Total lunar sample mass: 382 kg across all six missions. Six landing missions are correctly listed. Apollo 13 correctly noted as aborted.

lesson_title: Exploring the Moon: Origin, Far Side and Apollo
claim: Earth escape velocity ~11.2 km/s; Moon escape velocity ~2.4 km/s
notes: Earth: 11.186 km/s. Moon: 2.38 km/s. Both values correctly rounded.

lesson_title: The Sun: Structure, Fusion and Atmosphere
claim: Chromosphere extends to about 2,000 km above the photosphere and reaches temperatures of 20,000 K
notes: The chromosphere extends 2,000–3,000 km above the photosphere (range is stated correctly). However, temperatures in the upper chromosphere / transition region reach 50,000–100,000 K before jumping to coronal values of millions of K. The stated maximum of 20,000 K significantly undersells the chromosphere's upper temperature, which is commonly cited at up to ~50,000 K. For a GCSE audience the value is unlikely to be penalised but is a significant understatement compared to IAU/NASA sources. Recommend revising to '…up to approximately 50,000 K at its uppermost boundary'.

lesson_title: The Sun: Structure, Fusion and Atmosphere
claim: The Sun's core temperature is about 15 million K
notes: NASA/ESA: ~15 million K (15.7 × 10^6 K). Correct.

lesson_title: Sunspots, the Solar Cycle and the Solar Wind
claim: Maunder Minimum approximately 1645–1715
notes: Standard dates for the Maunder Minimum. Eddy (1976) defined 1645–1715. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Sunspots, the Solar Cycle and the Solar Wind
claim: 1989 Quebec blackout affected six million people for nine hours
notes: The March 1989 geomagnetic storm caused the Hydro-Québec collapse affecting ~6 million people for approximately 9 hours. Confirmed.

lesson_title: The Solar System: Planets, Dwarf Planets and Small Bodies
claim: Halley's Comet period ~75–76 years; last appeared 1986; returns ~2061
notes: Halley's period varies 74–79 years. Last perihelion: February 1986. Next perihelion: July 2061. All values correct.

lesson_title: Telescopes: Optics, Magnification and Resolution
claim: Galileo began systematic telescopic astronomy from 1609 and discovered: phases of Venus, four Galilean moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto), mountains on Moon, sunspots
notes: Galileo's first telescopic observations: late 1609. Sidereus Nuncius published March 1610. Four Galilean moons correctly named. Phases of Venus observed ~late 1610. Sunspots observed systematically from 1610–1611. All attributions correct.

lesson_title: Telescopes: Optics, Magnification and Resolution
claim: Hubble Space Telescope suffered spherical aberration at launch (1990), corrected with COSTAR in 1993
notes: HST launched April 1990. Spherical aberration confirmed June 1990. COSTAR installed December 1993 during STS-61 servicing mission. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Space Probes and Crewed Exploration
claim: New Horizons performed a historic fly-by of Pluto in July 2015
notes: New Horizons closest approach to Pluto: 14 July 2015. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Space Probes and Crewed Exploration
claim: Juno entered Jupiter's orbit in 2016
notes: Juno Jupiter orbit insertion: 4 July 2016. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Space Probes and Crewed Exploration
claim: Rosetta's Philae lander landed on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko in November 2014
notes: Philae landed 12 November 2014. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Space Probes and Crewed Exploration
claim: Apollo 8 (December 1968) was first crewed mission to orbit the Moon
notes: Apollo 8 launched 21 December 1968, entered lunar orbit 24 December 1968. First crewed lunar orbit. Confirmed.

lesson_title: Formation of Planetary Systems and Gravitational Forces
claim: Mercury escape velocity 4.3 km/s; Mars escape velocity 5.0 km/s
notes: Mercury: 4.25 km/s (rounds to 4.3 km/s). Mars: 5.03 km/s (rounds to 5.0 km/s). Both correctly stated.

lesson_title: Magnitude, Distance and Stellar Spectra
claim: Spectral classification OBAFGKM, hottest (O) to coolest (M); Sun is G-type at ~5,800 K
notes: OBAFGKM sequence is correct. Sun spectral type G2V, photosphere ~5,778 K. All correct.

lesson_title: Magnitude, Distance and Stellar Spectra
claim: 51 Pegasi b confirmed in 1995 as first exoplanet around a Sun-like star
notes: Mayor & Queloz announced 51 Peg b in October 1995. First confirmed exoplanet around a main-sequence Sun-like star. Correct.

lesson_title: The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram and Variable Stars
claim: Henrietta Swan Leavitt discovered the Cepheid period-luminosity relation in 1908
notes: Leavitt published a catalogue of 1,777 variable stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud in 1908 (Harvard College Observatory Circular 173) — this listed periods and apparent magnitudes but did NOT explicitly state the period-luminosity law. The period-luminosity relationship was formally announced in her 1912 paper (Harvard College Observatory Circular 173 note and then the 1912 paper by Leavitt & Pickering). The lesson says she 'discovered in 1908 that the pulsation period is directly related to the star's luminosity' — this misattributes the 1912 result to 1908. Recommended fix: 'Henrietta Swan Leavitt published the period-luminosity relation in 1912' (or 'first noted the relationship in 1908 and formally published it in 1912').

lesson_title: Stellar Evolution: Birth, Life and Death of Stars
claim: Bayer system: 'the brightest star in a constellation is labelled with the Greek letter alpha, the second brightest with beta'
notes: This is presented as a firm rule, but Bayer's assignment was only roughly by brightness and has many exceptions. The lesson itself immediately gives the counter-example: 'beta Orionis (Rigel) is the second-brightest in Orion' — but Rigel (β Ori, magnitude ~0.13) is actually brighter than Betelgeuse (α Ori, magnitude ~0.42–1.60 variable). Bayer appears to have assigned α to Betelgeuse and β to Rigel despite Rigel being brighter, possibly because Betelgeuse was brighter at the time of observation or for other reasons. The lesson should clarify that the Bayer assignment is approximate/historical and has exceptions, rather than stating it as a consistent brightness-ranking rule.

lesson_title: Stellar Evolution: Birth, Life and Death of Stars
claim: Chandrasekhar limit is 1.4 solar masses; Chandrasekhar 'calculated in 1930'
notes: Chandrasekhar derived the limit during his voyage to England in 1930 and published it in 1931. The 1.4 M☉ value is correct. Stating '1930' for the calculation is accurate.

lesson_title: Stellar Evolution: Birth, Life and Death of Stars
claim: New General Catalogue compiled by John Dreyer in 1888 lists nearly 8,000 objects
notes: NGC published 1888 by J.L.E. Dreyer with 7,840 entries. 'Nearly 8,000' is an accurate characterisation.

lesson_title: The Milky Way and Other Galaxies
claim: Milky Way classification is SBc in the Hubble tuning fork (key-fact box)
notes: The Milky Way's morphological classification is debated. Many sources cite SBbc (intermediate between SBb and SBc) rather than SBc. The main lesson text correctly states 'SBb' (in the galaxy types list), but the closing key-fact box states 'The Milky Way is an SBc — a loose-armed barred spiral'. This internal contradiction creates a factual inconsistency. SBbc or SBb are more commonly cited in peer-reviewed sources (e.g., Rix & Bovy 2013; NASA). SBc implies looser arms than most models suggest. Recommend standardising to SBbc or SBb, and removing the contradictory SBc from the key-fact box.

lesson_title: The Milky Way and Other Galaxies
claim: Andromeda Galaxy (M31) is approximately 2.5 million light-years from Earth and approaching at ~110 km/s
notes: Distance: 2.537 million ly (McConnachie 2012). Approaching at ~110 km/s radial velocity. Both values confirmed.

lesson_title: Cosmology: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
claim: Hubble published his finding in 1929; H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc
notes: Hubble (1929) 'A Relation between Distance and Radial Velocity among Extra-Galactic Nebulae'. Current consensus H₀ ~67–73 km/s/Mpc. 70 km/s/Mpc is a reasonable mid-range educational value. The Hubble tension collapsible correctly notes the 67 vs 73 tension.

lesson_title: Cosmology: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
claim: Age of universe approximately 13.8 billion years
notes: Planck 2018: 13.787 ± 0.020 Gyr. Correctly stated as 13.8 Gyr.

lesson_title: Cosmology: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
claim: CMB at approximately 2.7 K, discovered 1965 by Penzias and Wilson
notes: CMB temperature: 2.7255 ± 0.0006 K (Fixsen 2009). '2.7 K' is correct rounding. Penzias & Wilson discovered it in 1964–1965 (published 1965). Correct.

lesson_title: Cosmology: Redshift, Hubble's Law and the Big Bang
claim: Dark matter ~27%, dark energy ~68% of total energy density
notes: Planck 2018: dark energy 68.3%, dark matter 26.8%, baryonic matter 4.9%. Both stated values are correct to the given precision.
